source.title: Guide for Defense (G4D): Dynamic Guidance for Robust and Balanced Defense in Large Language Models
source.authors: He Cao; Weidi Luo; Yu Wang; Zi-Jing Liu; Bing Feng; Yuan Yao; Yu Li

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-completion rates under named jailbreak attack benchmarks, conceptually testing whether attacks can bypass model safety. It does not measure the specific token-position mechanism or fine-tuning interventions in the claim.
record.gate_note: Rows record No Defense attack-success rates. The paper also reports results for multiple defense methods, but those are evaluations of the paper’s defense system and baselines, not tests of the claim’s fine-tuning, token-position, or parameter-localization mechanisms. Direct CB-RedTeam harmful prompts are not included because they do not test getting past an opening, suffix, or decoding change.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper for its G4D inference-stage framework. The No Defense jailbreak ASRs are only baselines for judging the defense. The general-attack subset was chosen as attacks that already succeeded on GPT-3.5, GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3-8B, so GPT-4o-mini's rates are partly fixed by that selection. Most attacks (DeepInception, PAIR, AutoDAN templates) are prompt rewrites, not prefilling, suffix or decoding changes. The paper makes no argument about whether getting past the opening tokens bypasses safety. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The authors conclude that G4D, a three-agent inference-stage defense (intention detection with retrieval, paraphrasing, safety guidance), lowers jailbreak and domain-specific (CB-RedTeam) ASR while preserving benign performance, works across agent LLMs, and can be combined with output-stage defenses.
record.recipe_differences: No fine-tuning or token-distribution recipe is tested; G4D is an inference-stage, multi-agent defense.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies by model, attack benchmark, and prompt set (the main subset versus the total set).
record.problems: The general-attack main results use a subset selected for attacks that succeeded on GPT-3.5, GPT-4o-mini, and Llama-3-8B; the paper also reports total-set results for Vicuna-v1.5-13B. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The tested attack benchmarks do not isolate the opening-token mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted defense-method comparison rows in Table 2 and Appendix Table 9 because they report the performance of defense interventions rather than additional no-defense attack outcomes. Omitted CB-RedTeam direct harmful-prompt ASRs in Table 2 because those prompts do not test an opening, suffix, or decoding bypass.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling or decoding manipulation. Suffix attacks (GCG, SAA) appear only as baseline ASRs for the defense, with no isolation of the opening-token bypass.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.
No deepening training. G4D is an input-side prompting defense.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misaligned Table 2's columns: the order is CB-RedTeam, GCG, DeepInception, SAA, PAIR, AutoDAN. This is confirmed by the text (Vicuna CB-RedTeam 53% to 1.3%, G4D GCG 16.7%, AutoDAN 2.5%, PAIR 11.1% on GPT-4o-mini) and by Tables 5, 7 and 9. As a result, R1–R10 all carry wrong values, and the 'CB-RedTeam' figures the reader left out are the 45.3 and 53.3 it recorded as GCG. Even with corrected values these are baselines for a defense paper on success-selected subsets, so the study is reclassified as T4 with no verdicts. The subset sizes in Table 8 are garbled in the extracted text and cannot be reliably assigned to attacks.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning or example-count intervention.
No benign fine-tuning intervention or measurement of harmful compliance after such training.
No per-token KL or aligned-versus-base distribution measurement.

Tests general jailbreak attack benchmarks, but does not report compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes; the text does not specify whether the named GCG results are attributable to suffixes specifically.
No weight or rank localization intervention.
No test of why safety would be shallow, including data or objective effects.
No training intended to deepen safety across response positions.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Named jailbreak benchmarks with nonzero ASR in the no-defense setting
reader_labels.reason: The attacks produced harmful completions in both models on the reported subset; Vicuna-v1.5-13B also had 100% ASR for DeepInception. Rows R1-R10.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Attack success is incomplete in most reported model/attack conditions, and rates differ between prompt sets
reader_labels.reason: Most subset rates are below 100%; Vicuna’s total-set rates also differ from its subset rates across attack types. Rows R1-R6 and R8-R15.
